$description: How a component is built in a design file: each aspect lists the ways the studied libraries do it and the one Sketchbook adopts. Team-owned; sketchbook api practices shows it, check A1 validates it (decision SB-0079).

reference-c.name: A product design system studied for its approach

figma-docs.name: Figma help center and Plugin API reference

state-model.question: How are interaction, validity and availability expressed as variants?

flat-state.summary: One State axis lists everything: Enabled, Hover, Focus, Error, Warning, Read-only, Disabled, and even crossings such as Hover + Error.

interaction-state.summary: State holds only the interaction states the contract gives tokens for (Rest, Hover, Focus, Press, Loading); validity, availability and on/off are their own False/True or value axes.

state-model.reason: The combinations stay a product of independent axes instead of a growing list of crossings, and each State value maps to a contract state key in spec/api.json (states.draw).

optional-parts.question: How does a designer show or hide an optional part (description, value, icon)?

show-property.summary: A BOOLEAN property named 'Show <part>' toggles the layer.

part-property.summary: A BOOLEAN property named after the part itself ('Description', 'Left icon') toggles the layer.

optional-parts.reason: Names come from the registry's content keys, so the same word names the prop in code, the property in the file and the layer.

text-properties.question: How is the text a component shows exposed?

bare-name.summary: TEXT properties named after the part ('Label', 'ErrorText').

part-text.summary: TEXT properties named '<Part> text' ('Label text', 'Error text', 'Min range text').

text-properties.reason: A TEXT property and a BOOLEAN property for the same part (Description, Description text) would otherwise collide in the panel.

helper-parts.question: Where do shared pieces (rails, items, bases) live?

inline.summary: Layers inside the component; no helper components.

underscore-components.summary: A piece used by several variants or components is its own component named with a leading underscore (hidden from publishing) and described as not for independent use.

helper-parts.reason: Inline until a piece is shared by two or more components; then it becomes an underscore helper whose description is the fixed 'not for independent use' line.

nested-instances.question: How is a component built from another one?

nest-library-component.summary: The variant holds an instance of the other library component (a value input inside a slider, toggles inside a toggle group) with its properties set.

redraw.summary: The parts are drawn again inside each component.

nested-instances.reason: It follows the contract's dependsOn and keeps one source for each look.

content-regions.question: How is a region filled with the person's own content (a card body, a panel, row actions) drawn?

sample-text.summary: The region holds sample text; content is placed by detaching or by covering it.

native-slot.summary: The region is a native slot (a SLOT property spanning the set) with sample content and no limits; a few components are offered first as preferred values.

content-regions.reason: A slot takes any layer without detaching the instance, so the region stays linked to the library; preferred values point to the usual content without forbidding the rest.

exposed-instances.question: Are a nested instance's properties editable from the parent, and how is its layer named?

hidden-generic-names.summary: Nested instances stay closed; their layers keep part names (item, field-other).

expose-with-names.summary: Every nested library instance whose component has properties is exposed, so its properties show in the parent's panel, under the component's title and an index (Toggle 1, Button 2).

exposed-instances.reason: A designer sets each item of a group from the parent's panel instead of drilling into layers; an instance without properties would add an empty entry, so it is left closed.

drawn-content.question: How much of the control's visible content is drawn, and can it be edited?

chrome-only.summary: The frame, border and colors only; text and values are placeholders.

contract-content.summary: Every piece of visible content the contract defines (value, minimum, maximum, placeholder, label) is drawn with a TEXT property; positions that the value moves (a slider handle) are laid out so a designer can move them.

drawn-content.reason: A component that shows no value cannot be reviewed against the story that does.

page-layout.question: Where do the component, its helpers and its documentation sit?

page-per-component.summary: One page per component holding the set, its helpers and a specification frame with the states side by side.

library-page.summary: All sets on one Library page so instances resolve across components; documentation lives on separate Components pages, generated from the same source.

page-layout.reason: The design stamp (check D1) and the nested instances already rely on one Library page. The documentation step adds a generated page per component; revisit if the file outgrows one page.

description.question: What does a component's description say?

summary-and-notes.summary: A summary line and a few usage notes.

sectioned.summary: Sections: what it is, behavior, when to use, what not to do, and notes for generating code.

description.reason: After the API, the description is what the design tool's MCP hands to an agent. It is generated from contract.md, contract.json and the registry, never written in the file.

zero-values.question: Is a value of zero bound to a variable?

literal-zero.summary: Zeros are typed as numbers; the file reports them as unlinked values.

bound-none-step.summary: Each kind has a semantic zero (space, radius, border width, opacity) and a zero the component draws on purpose (a square inner corner, an unused stroke side, a joined group's gap) is bound to it.

zero-values.reason: Every value the file draws is then a token, scales start at 0, and a designer never sees an unlinked 0 to second-guess.

text-decoration.question: How is text drawn that one variant underlines (a link on hover)?

format-the-layer.summary: The variant's label layer is underlined by hand.

twin-style-and-layer.summary: Every text role has an underlined twin style; the component draws a second label layer on it, with its own text property, visible only where the variant underlines.

text-decoration.reason: Formatting on a layer bound to a TEXT property is shared by every variant of the set, so underlining one variant's label underlines them all.
